recommendation.message: GnRH antagonist protocol (fixed start Day 5–6) recommended for normal responder.

explanation.clinicalRationale: GnRH antagonist protocol with fixed start on stimulation Day 5 or 6 (ESHRE 2025 Rec 22, 23 / Grade A; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018) is recommended as first line for predicted normal responders. It achieves equivalent ongoing pregnancy and live birth rates to long agonist regimens while significantly reducing treatment duration, total gonadotropin consumption, and OHSS risk. Delayed-start stimulation is probably not recommended over conventional dosing (ESHRE 2025 Rec 15), and estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended in antagonist protocols (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Long GnRH agonist protocol remains an established alternative when precise cycle scheduling or clinic batching is required (Rec 21).
explanation.notes: Target follicular cohort: 8–14 oocytes. Conventional gonadotropin dose 150–225 IU/day.

selection.message: Recombinant FSH (r-hFSH) or hp-hMG equally recommended for ovarian stimulation in normal responders.
selection.lhStrategy: Routine LH supplementation is probably not recommended over r-hFSH alone for normal responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 28, Conditional, ⊕⊕).
negativeRecommendations: Combined use of r-hFSH with hMG is probably not recommended over either alone (ESHRE 2025 Rec 31, Conditional, ⊕⊕).
Do NOT add letrozole to stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 38, Conditional, ⊕).
Do NOT add clomiphene citrate to stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 41, Conditional, ⊕⊕⊕).
Do NOT add low-dose hCG to FSH stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 36, Conditional, ⊕).

explanation.whySelected: Recombinant FSH (r-hFSH) and human menopausal gonadotropin (hp-hMG) are equally recommended for ovarian stimulation in normal responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 25). Follitropin alfa, beta, and delta demonstrate equivalent clinical efficacy and live birth rates (Rec 33). In GnRH antagonist cycles, long-acting corifollitropin alfa is equally recommended to daily r-hFSH (Rec 32).

explanation.clinicalComments: Conventional starting dose of 150–225 IU/day is recommended (Rec 16). Follitropin delta and follitropin alfa/beta are equally recommended (Rec 33).

rule.triggerRuleName: hCG Trigger Criteria and Dose (Standard Final Maturation)
rule.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation 2020/2025; ASRM Guidelines
rule.population: Normal and expected poor ovarian responders with low OHSS risk (peak E2 < 3,000 pg/mL, < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm) undergoing fresh embryo transfer.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist or Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocols
rule.hormonalCriteria: Concordant serum Estradiol (approx. 150–250 pg/mL per mature follicle ≥ 14 mm); Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar appearance for fresh embryo transfer
rule.safetyCriteria: Peak Estradiol < 3,000–3,500 pg/mL; < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm; absence of early OHSS symptoms
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 37 hours (standard 36 hours) prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Recombinant hCG (Choriogonadotropin alfa) 250 µg s.c. (equiv. ~6,500 IU) or urinary hCG 5,000–10,000 IU s.c. (10,000 IU for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
contraindications: High risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm)
History of severe early-onset OHSS
exceptions: Cases converted to elective freeze-all can receive hCG if agonist trigger is contraindicated (e.g. pituitary defect) with cabergoline prophylaxis
rule.action: Administer rhCG 250 µg s.c. 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh cleavage-stage or blastocyst transfer.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / High Quality RCT Evidence
potentialAdvantages: Gold standard for fresh embryo transfer with robust, well-established luteal phase support
Consistent LH receptor activation ensuring high oocyte maturation and blastulation rates in normal responders
potentialLimitations: Prolonged half-life (elimination half-life ~30–36 hours) sustained over 8–10 days
Significantly increases OHSS risk in hyper-responders due to continuous luteotropic VEGF production
safetyConsiderations: Strict avoidance in patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18 follicles ≥ 10 mm
Progesterone measurement recommended on trigger day to rule out premature luteinization (P4 ≥ 1.5 ng/mL)

rule.triggerRuleName: GnRH Agonist Trigger Criteria and Dose (OHSS Prevention)
rule.source: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
rule.publication: Cochrane Database Syst Rev / Fertil Steril
rule.population: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist protocol ONLY (intact, non-downregulated pituitary GnRH receptors required)
rule.hormonalCriteria: Peak Estradiol typically > 3,500 pg/mL or rapid follicular cohort proliferation
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial lining receptivity not primary concern due to planned total cryopreservation
rule.safetyCriteria: Virtually eliminates both early-onset and late-onset severe OHSS by inducing rapid luteolysis
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocol (pituitary receptors desensitized; will fail to elicit LH surge)
Hypothalamic hypogonadism (deficient endogenous gonadotropin stores)
exceptions: Fresh transfer can be performed only if low-dose hCG luteal rescue (1,500 IU) or intensive luteal phase support (high-dose progesterone + estradiol) is administered
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / Cochrane Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
potentialAdvantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
potentialLimitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)

rule.triggerRuleName: Dual Trigger (GnRH Agonist + Low-Dose hCG) Criteria and Dose
rule.source: Clinical Evidence & ESHRE/ASRM Consensus (Griffin 2014; Lin 2013; Ding 2020)
rule.population: Normal responders in GnRH antagonist protocol planning fresh transfer, or patients with previous low oocyte maturation rate (MII < 60%), POSEIDON groups, or poor responder cohorts.
rule.hormonalCriteria: Estradiol < 3,500 pg/mL, Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar pattern
rule.safetyCriteria: Moderate or low OHSS risk (avoid in severe hyper-responders with > 25 follicles)
rule.timingCriteria: Administer both agents simultaneously 35 to 37 hours prior to oocyte retrieval
rule.doseCriteria: GnRH Agonist (Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c.) PLUS low-dose hCG (1,000–1,500 IU s.c. or rhCG 65–125 µg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation cycles
Severe OHSS risk (E2 > 4,500 pg/mL or > 25 follicles) where all exogenous hCG must be avoided
exceptions: In high normal responders, the hCG component may be halved to 1,000 IU
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg + hCG 1,000–1,500 IU s.c. simultaneously 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh embryo transfer.
potentialAdvantages: Significantly increases percentage of mature metaphase II (MII) oocytes and usable blastocysts in suboptimal responders
Permits fresh embryo transfer with standard luteal support while lowering OHSS risk relative to full-dose hCG (10,000 IU)
potentialLimitations: Contains low-dose hCG, which retains small residual OHSS risk compared to pure agonist trigger in hyper-responders
safetyConsiderations: Do not use if trigger day Estradiol exceeds 4,000 pg/mL or total follicle count exceeds 22 follicles

fields.label: Primary recommendation
fields.value: GnRH antagonist protocol with fixed start on stimulation Day 5 or 6 (ESHRE 2025 Rec 22, 23 / Grade A; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018) is recommended as first line for predicted normal responders. It achieves equivalent ongoing pregnancy and live birth rates to long agonist regimens while significantly reducing treatment duration, total gonadotropin consumption, and OHSS risk. Delayed-start stimulation is probably not recommended over conventional dosing (ESHRE 2025 Rec 15), and estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended in antagonist protocols (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Long GnRH agonist protocol remains an established alternative when precise cycle scheduling or clinic batching is required (Rec 21).

fields.label: Primary recommendation
fields.value: Recombinant FSH (r-hFSH) and human menopausal gonadotropin (hp-hMG) are equally recommended for ovarian stimulation in normal responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 25). Follitropin alfa, beta, and delta demonstrate equivalent clinical efficacy and live birth rates (Rec 33). In GnRH antagonist cycles, long-acting corifollitropin alfa is equally recommended to daily r-hFSH (Rec 32).

explanations.name: Bologna Poor-Responder Engine
explanations.evaluated: Whether the recorded data satisfy the ESHRE Bologna definition of poor ovarian response (Ferraretti 2011).
inputs: Advanced maternal age or a risk factor for poor response
reasoning: Only 0 of the three published features is present; the consensus requires at least two, and fewer than two episodes of poor response are recorded.
Advanced maternal age or a risk factor for poor response: Maternal age 30 years — below 40, and no risk factor for poor response is documented.
Previous poor ovarian response: Lowest recorded oocyte yield is 10 — above the ≤ 3 oocyte threshold.
Abnormal ovarian reserve test: Ovarian reserve testing is not abnormal by the published range: AMH 2.5 ng/mL (at or above the 0.5–1.1 ng/mL range); AFC 15 (at or above the 5–7 follicle range).

evidence.title: A new more detailed stratification of low responders to ovarian stimulation: from a poor ovarian response to a low prognosis concept
authors: POSEIDON Group (Patient-Oriented Strategies Encompassing IndividualizeD Oocyte Number)
evidence.summary: Original POSEIDON statement defining the low-prognosis concept and the four groups based on female age (<35 vs ≥35 years), ovarian reserve markers (AFC ≥5 / AMH ≥1.2 ng/mL) and ovarian response to previous conventional stimulation (<4 oocytes = poor; 4-9 oocytes = suboptimal).

evidence.title: The novel POSEIDON stratification of 'Low prognosis patients in Assisted Reproductive Technology' and its proposed marker of successful outcome
evidence.summary: Detailed description of the POSEIDON stratification, including sub-groups 1a/1b and 2a/2b and the rationale for separating expected from unexpected low ovarian response.

evidence.title: ESHRE consensus on the definition of 'poor response' to ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization: the Bologna criteria
authors: ESHRE working group on Poor Ovarian Response Definition
evidence.summary: ESHRE consensus establishing a standardised definition of poor ovarian response for research and clinical reporting, based on advanced maternal age or a risk factor, a previous poor response and abnormal ovarian reserve testing.

evidence.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI
evidence.summary: European society guideline on ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI. The guideline development group formulated 84 recommendations answering 18 key questions covering pre-stimulation assessment, prediction of ovarian response, stimulation regimens, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering and luteal support.

evidence.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM Practice Committee opinion describing the available ovarian reserve tests, their performance characteristics and the limitations of using them to counsel patients.

evidence.title: Prevention and treatment of moderate and severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome: a guideline
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM guideline reviewing the evidence on identification of patients at risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and on the strategies studied for its prevention and management.

evidence.title: Ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI — ESHRE guideline, update 2025
authors: The ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation
evidence.publisher: Oxford University Press / European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology
evidence.summary: November 2025 update of the ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline. Structured in parts covering pre-stimulation evaluation (ovarian response and pregnancy prediction from AFC, AMH, basal FSH, inhibin B, oestradiol, progesterone, LH, age and BMI), pre-treatment therapies, stimulation regimens and gonadotrophin choice, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering, luteal phase support and cycle-cancellation considerations. Recommendation statements are transcribed into modules only after specialist review.

evidence.title: Gonadotrophin-releasing hormone antagonists for assisted reproductive technology
evidence.summary: Cochrane review comparing GnRH antagonist protocols with long GnRH agonist protocols across randomised trials, reporting live birth, ongoing pregnancy and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome outcomes.

evidence.title: Usability and utility of the CONSORT calculator for FSH starting doses: a prospective observational study
evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre observational study (197 women, 45 French centres) of the CONSORT calculator in routine practice. Full text uploaded and verified: it confirms the four calculator inputs (age, BMI, cycle day 2-4 basal FSH, AFC of follicles >=2 mm and <11 mm), the recommendation range of 112.5-450 IU in 37.5 IU increments, and that the calculator was delivered as a password-protected website rather than a printed table. It prints NO variable bands, NO point assignments and NO score-to-dose crosswalk. Usability was high (97.8% of physicians) but the recommendation was followed for only 45.2% of patients; mean CONSORT dose 119.7 IU versus 163.9 IU planned and 151.7 IU prescribed.

recommendation.message: GnRH antagonist protocol recommended for poor ovarian responder / POSEIDON profile.

explanation.clinicalRationale: GnRH antagonist protocol is recommended for predicted poor responders, POSEIDON groups, and Bologna criteria (ESHRE 2025 Rec 18, 22; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018). The antagonist avoids profound pituitary downregulation and heavy suppression of early follicular recruitment, reducing stimulation duration and gonadotropin consumption with equivalent live birth rates. Starting dose is strictly capped at the 300 IU/day hard ceiling per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20 (Strong recommendation, High Quality). Delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 17), and routine estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Microflare (short agonist flare) is an alternative to utilize endogenous flare. In very low reserve, modified natural cycle may be considered per ESHRE 2025 Rec 19 (GPP).

selection.message: Highly purified hMG (hp-hMG) or r-hFSH with r-hLH recommended for advanced reproductive age (≥35 years) and poor ovarian reserve.
selection.lhStrategy: LH supplementation (via hp-hMG or r-hLH addition) is equally recommended to r-hFSH alone for women of advanced age (≥35 years) and low responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 29, 30). Compensates for age-related decline in theca-cell LH sensitivity.
negativeRecommendations: Do NOT combine r-hFSH and hMG concurrently in the same stimulation phase (ESHRE 2025 Rec 31, Conditional, ⊕⊕).
A gonadotropin daily dose higher than 300 IU/day is NOT recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 20, Strong, ⊕).
Adding low dosages of hCG to FSH stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 36, Conditional, ⊕).
Routine letrozole addition is probably not recommended for low responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 39, Conditional, ⊕⊕).

explanation.whySelected: Highly purified hMG (hp-hMG) is recommended as a preferred preparation for women of advanced reproductive age (≥35 years) and low ovarian reserve (POSEIDON Groups 2/4, Bologna POR). Provides dual FSH and LH/hCG activity in a single preparation. Recombinant FSH with r-hLH or fixed combination (2:1) is an equally recommended alternative (ESHRE 2025 Rec 25, 29, 30).
explanation.supportingPublication: Ata B. et al., Hum Reprod Open 2025; Alviggi C. et al., Front Endocrinol 2016
explanation.clinicalComments: Daily gonadotropin dose must not exceed 300 IU/day (ESHRE Rec 20). If mild stimulation is selected, clomiphene citrate alone or with gonadotropins is equally recommended (Rec 42). Routine growth hormone, DHEA, or testosterone are probably not recommended (Rec 47, 49, 50).

registeredRules.ruleName: Hypo-Response / Slow Follicular Recruitment — Step-Up Titration (POSEIDON / ESHRE Rec 20)
registeredRules.source: POSEIDON Group Stratification (Alviggi et al., 2016) / ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.population: Suboptimal or slow responders on Day 5–8 of ovarian stimulation
registeredRules.gonadotropin: r-hFSH or hMG (or addition of LH activity)
registeredRules.threshold: Stimulation Day >= 5 with lead follicle < 10 mm OR <= 2 follicles >= 10 mm OR E2 < 180 pg/mL
registeredRules.action: Increase gonadotropin dose by +50 to +75 IU/day up to maximum ceiling of 300 IU/day (never exceed 300 IU/day per ESHRE Rec 20). If already at 300 IU/day, maintain dose and assess follicular viability.
exceptions: Patients already receiving 300 IU/day ceiling dose
contraindications: Doses > 300 IU/day are contraindicated per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.evidenceLevel: Level II (Strong recommendation for 300 IU ceiling)

registeredRules.ruleName: Excessive Follicular Cohort / Rapid Estradiol Surge — Step-Down / Coasting (ASRM 2016 / ESHRE 2025)
registeredRules.source: ASRM OHSS Prevention Guideline (2016) / ESHRE 2025 Guideline Update
registeredRules.population: Predicted high responders and patients exhibiting explosive follicular kinetics or OHSS hazard
registeredRules.threshold: >= 18 follicles >= 10 mm OR Estradiol > 3000 pg/mL on Day 6–8 (or > 4000 pg/mL approaching trigger)
registeredRules.action: Reduce daily gonadotropin dose by 25–50 IU/day (floor 75–100 IU/day). If E2 > 4000–5000 pg/mL, consider coasting for 1–2 days while continuing antagonist. Prepare GnRH agonist trigger and elective freeze-all.
registeredRules.doseChange: -25 to -50 IU/day (or coasting if E2 >= 4500 pg/mL)
exceptions: End of stimulation when follicles are already trigger-ready (>= 17 mm)
contraindications: Do not administer hCG trigger if E2 > 4000 pg/mL or > 18 follicles >= 11 mm; agonist trigger required

registeredRules.ruleName: Cohort Maturation Reached — Discontinue Gonadotropins & Trigger (ESHRE 2025 Rec 83/84)

registeredRules.population: All patients reaching follicular trigger criteria
registeredRules.threshold: >= 3 follicles >= 17 mm OR lead follicle >= 18 mm (or >= 17 mm in low prognosis)
registeredRules.action: Stimulation complete. Discontinue daily gonadotropin injections and proceed immediately to final oocyte maturation triggering.

rule.triggerRuleName: hCG Trigger Criteria and Dose (Standard Final Maturation)
rule.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation 2020/2025; ASRM Guidelines
rule.population: Normal and expected poor ovarian responders with low OHSS risk (peak E2 < 3,000 pg/mL, < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm) undergoing fresh embryo transfer.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist or Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocols
rule.hormonalCriteria: Concordant serum Estradiol (approx. 150–250 pg/mL per mature follicle ≥ 14 mm); Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar appearance for fresh embryo transfer
rule.safetyCriteria: Peak Estradiol < 3,000–3,500 pg/mL; < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm; absence of early OHSS symptoms
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 37 hours (standard 36 hours) prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Recombinant hCG (Choriogonadotropin alfa) 250 µg s.c. (equiv. ~6,500 IU) or urinary hCG 5,000–10,000 IU s.c. (10,000 IU for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
contraindications: High risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm)
History of severe early-onset OHSS
exceptions: Cases converted to elective freeze-all can receive hCG if agonist trigger is contraindicated (e.g. pituitary defect) with cabergoline prophylaxis
rule.action: Administer rhCG 250 µg s.c. 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh cleavage-stage or blastocyst transfer.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / High Quality RCT Evidence
potentialAdvantages: Gold standard for fresh embryo transfer with robust, well-established luteal phase support
Consistent LH receptor activation ensuring high oocyte maturation and blastulation rates in normal responders
potentialLimitations: Prolonged half-life (elimination half-life ~30–36 hours) sustained over 8–10 days
Significantly increases OHSS risk in hyper-responders due to continuous luteotropic VEGF production
safetyConsiderations: Strict avoidance in patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18 follicles ≥ 10 mm
Progesterone measurement recommended on trigger day to rule out premature luteinization (P4 ≥ 1.5 ng/mL)

rule.triggerRuleName: GnRH Agonist Trigger Criteria and Dose (OHSS Prevention)
rule.source: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
rule.publication: Cochrane Database Syst Rev / Fertil Steril
rule.population: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist protocol ONLY (intact, non-downregulated pituitary GnRH receptors required)
rule.hormonalCriteria: Peak Estradiol typically > 3,500 pg/mL or rapid follicular cohort proliferation
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial lining receptivity not primary concern due to planned total cryopreservation
rule.safetyCriteria: Virtually eliminates both early-onset and late-onset severe OHSS by inducing rapid luteolysis
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocol (pituitary receptors desensitized; will fail to elicit LH surge)
Hypothalamic hypogonadism (deficient endogenous gonadotropin stores)
exceptions: Fresh transfer can be performed only if low-dose hCG luteal rescue (1,500 IU) or intensive luteal phase support (high-dose progesterone + estradiol) is administered
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / Cochrane Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
potentialAdvantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
potentialLimitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)

rule.triggerRuleName: Dual Trigger (GnRH Agonist + Low-Dose hCG) Criteria and Dose
rule.source: Clinical Evidence & ESHRE/ASRM Consensus (Griffin 2014; Lin 2013; Ding 2020)
rule.population: Normal responders in GnRH antagonist protocol planning fresh transfer, or patients with previous low oocyte maturation rate (MII < 60%), POSEIDON groups, or poor responder cohorts.
rule.hormonalCriteria: Estradiol < 3,500 pg/mL, Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar pattern
rule.safetyCriteria: Moderate or low OHSS risk (avoid in severe hyper-responders with > 25 follicles)
rule.timingCriteria: Administer both agents simultaneously 35 to 37 hours prior to oocyte retrieval
rule.doseCriteria: GnRH Agonist (Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c.) PLUS low-dose hCG (1,000–1,500 IU s.c. or rhCG 65–125 µg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation cycles
Severe OHSS risk (E2 > 4,500 pg/mL or > 25 follicles) where all exogenous hCG must be avoided
exceptions: In high normal responders, the hCG component may be halved to 1,000 IU
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg + hCG 1,000–1,500 IU s.c. simultaneously 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh embryo transfer.
potentialAdvantages: Significantly increases percentage of mature metaphase II (MII) oocytes and usable blastocysts in suboptimal responders
Permits fresh embryo transfer with standard luteal support while lowering OHSS risk relative to full-dose hCG (10,000 IU)
potentialLimitations: Contains low-dose hCG, which retains small residual OHSS risk compared to pure agonist trigger in hyper-responders
safetyConsiderations: Do not use if trigger day Estradiol exceeds 4,000 pg/mL or total follicle count exceeds 22 follicles

fields.label: Primary recommendation
fields.value: GnRH antagonist protocol is recommended for predicted poor responders, POSEIDON groups, and Bologna criteria (ESHRE 2025 Rec 18, 22; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018). The antagonist avoids profound pituitary downregulation and heavy suppression of early follicular recruitment, reducing stimulation duration and gonadotropin consumption with equivalent live birth rates. Starting dose is strictly capped at the 300 IU/day hard ceiling per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20 (Strong recommendation, High Quality). Delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 17), and routine estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Microflare (short agonist flare) is an alternative to utilize endogenous flare. In very low reserve, modified natural cycle may be considered per ESHRE 2025 Rec 19 (GPP).

evidence.title: Usability and utility of the CONSORT calculator for FSH starting doses: a prospective observational study
evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre observational study (197 women, 45 French centres) of the CONSORT calculator in routine practice. Full text uploaded and verified: it confirms the four calculator inputs (age, BMI, cycle day 2-4 basal FSH, AFC of follicles >=2 mm and <11 mm), the recommendation range of 112.5-450 IU in 37.5 IU increments, and that the calculator was delivered as a password-protected website rather than a printed table. It prints NO variable bands, NO point assignments and NO score-to-dose crosswalk. Usability was high (97.8% of physicians) but the recommendation was followed for only 45.2% of patients; mean CONSORT dose 119.7 IU versus 163.9 IU planned and 151.7 IU prescribed.

recommendation.message: GnRH antagonist protocol recommended for high responder / PCOS / OHSS risk profile.

explanation.clinicalRationale: GnRH antagonist protocol is strongly recommended for predicted high responders and PCOS patients (ESHRE 2025 Rec 14 / Grade A; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514). Antagonist protocols yield equivalent live birth rates compared to long agonist protocols while reducing moderate-to-severe OHSS by over 50%, and uniquely allow GnRH agonist triggering. Starting dose explicitly defaults to the 100–125 IU/day tier per ESHRE 2025 Rec 13. Routine delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 12), and estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended in antagonist protocols (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Long agonist protocols are contraindicated due to unmitigated OHSS risk. PPOS is an evidence-supported alternative (ESHRE 2025 Rec 24) when elective freeze-all or PGT-A is planned.
explanation.notes: Strict OHSS surveillance indicated. Default starting dose 100–125 IU/day. Agonist trigger and freeze-all strategy should be prepared.

selection.message: Recombinant human FSH (r-hFSH) recommended to enable precise pen dose titration and avoid exogenous LH activity in high OHSS risk.
selection.lhStrategy: No LH supplementation indicated. Pure FSH preparation is preferred; avoid exogenous LH/hCG activity to minimize excessive steroidogenesis and reduce OHSS risk (ESHRE 2025 Rec 28).
negativeRecommendations: Do NOT add letrozole to gonadotropin stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 37, Conditional, ⊕).
Do NOT add clomiphene citrate to gonadotropin stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 40, Conditional, ⊕⊕).
Do NOT add low-dose hCG to FSH stimulation (ESHRE 2025 Rec 36, Conditional, ⊕).
Concurrent combination of r-hFSH with hMG is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 31, Conditional, ⊕⊕).

explanation.whySelected: Recombinant FSH (r-hFSH) is recommended as the primary gonadotropin for predicted high responders and women with PCOS. Multi-dose pen injectors allow fine-increment dose titration (12.5–25 IU) to adhere strictly to reduced starting doses (100–150 IU/day per ESHRE Rec 13) and avoid excessive follicular recruitment.
explanation.supportingPublication: Ata B. et al., Hum Reprod Open 2025; ASRM Practice Committee, Fertil Steril 2016
explanation.clinicalComments: Follitropin delta and follitropin alfa/beta are equally recommended (ESHRE Rec 33). GnRH antagonist protocol is strongly recommended (Rec 14). Strict freeze-all is indicated if estradiol exceeds 3,500 pg/mL or follicle count exceeds 18.

doseAdjustment.rationale: Marked hyper-response with critical estradiol elevation (E2 >= 4,500 pg/mL or >= 18 follicles >= 10 mm). Withhold gonadotropins for 1–2 days (coasting) while maintaining daily GnRH antagonist (0.25 mg), or reduce dose to 75–100 IU/day. Mandatory GnRH agonist trigger and elective freeze-all indicated to eliminate OHSS risk.

firedRule.ruleName: Excessive Follicular Cohort / Rapid Estradiol Surge — Step-Down / Coasting (ASRM 2016 / ESHRE 2025)
firedRule.source: ASRM OHSS Prevention Guideline (2016) / ESHRE 2025 Guideline Update
firedRule.population: Predicted high responders and patients exhibiting explosive follicular kinetics or OHSS hazard
firedRule.threshold: >= 18 follicles >= 10 mm OR Estradiol > 3000 pg/mL on Day 6–8 (or > 4000 pg/mL approaching trigger)
firedRule.action: Reduce daily gonadotropin dose by 25–50 IU/day (floor 75–100 IU/day). If E2 > 4000–5000 pg/mL, consider coasting for 1–2 days while continuing antagonist. Prepare GnRH agonist trigger and elective freeze-all.
firedRule.doseChange: -25 to -50 IU/day (or coasting if E2 >= 4500 pg/mL)
exceptions: End of stimulation when follicles are already trigger-ready (>= 17 mm)
contraindications: Do not administer hCG trigger if E2 > 4000 pg/mL or > 18 follicles >= 11 mm; agonist trigger required

rule.triggerRuleName: hCG Trigger Criteria and Dose (Standard Final Maturation)
rule.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation 2020/2025; ASRM Guidelines
rule.population: Normal and expected poor ovarian responders with low OHSS risk (peak E2 < 3,000 pg/mL, < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm) undergoing fresh embryo transfer.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist or Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocols
rule.hormonalCriteria: Concordant serum Estradiol (approx. 150–250 pg/mL per mature follicle ≥ 14 mm); Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar appearance for fresh embryo transfer
rule.safetyCriteria: Peak Estradiol < 3,000–3,500 pg/mL; < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm; absence of early OHSS symptoms
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 37 hours (standard 36 hours) prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Recombinant hCG (Choriogonadotropin alfa) 250 µg s.c. (equiv. ~6,500 IU) or urinary hCG 5,000–10,000 IU s.c. (10,000 IU for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
contraindications: High risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm)
History of severe early-onset OHSS
exceptions: Cases converted to elective freeze-all can receive hCG if agonist trigger is contraindicated (e.g. pituitary defect) with cabergoline prophylaxis
rule.action: Administer rhCG 250 µg s.c. 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh cleavage-stage or blastocyst transfer.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / High Quality RCT Evidence
potentialAdvantages: Gold standard for fresh embryo transfer with robust, well-established luteal phase support
Consistent LH receptor activation ensuring high oocyte maturation and blastulation rates in normal responders
potentialLimitations: Prolonged half-life (elimination half-life ~30–36 hours) sustained over 8–10 days
Significantly increases OHSS risk in hyper-responders due to continuous luteotropic VEGF production
safetyConsiderations: Strict avoidance in patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18 follicles ≥ 10 mm
Progesterone measurement recommended on trigger day to rule out premature luteinization (P4 ≥ 1.5 ng/mL)
rule.activationPoint: src/lib/engine/trigger.ts — activated with ESHRE 2025 and ASRM validated criteria.

rule.triggerRuleName: GnRH Agonist Trigger Criteria and Dose (OHSS Prevention)
rule.source: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
rule.publication: Cochrane Database Syst Rev / Fertil Steril
rule.population: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist protocol ONLY (intact, non-downregulated pituitary GnRH receptors required)
rule.hormonalCriteria: Peak Estradiol typically > 3,500 pg/mL or rapid follicular cohort proliferation
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial lining receptivity not primary concern due to planned total cryopreservation
rule.safetyCriteria: Virtually eliminates both early-onset and late-onset severe OHSS by inducing rapid luteolysis
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocol (pituitary receptors desensitized; will fail to elicit LH surge)
Hypothalamic hypogonadism (deficient endogenous gonadotropin stores)
exceptions: Fresh transfer can be performed only if low-dose hCG luteal rescue (1,500 IU) or intensive luteal phase support (high-dose progesterone + estradiol) is administered
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / Cochrane Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
potentialAdvantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
potentialLimitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)

options.applicabilityDetail: Strongly Recommended (ESHRE Grade A / ASRM): Antagonist cycle with elevated OHSS risk. Agonist trigger + Freeze-All virtually eliminates severe OHSS.
options.validatedPopulation: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
advantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
limitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)
options.sourceLabel: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
options.doseStatus: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
options.timingStatus: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
options.evidenceSupportedAction: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.

rule.triggerRuleName: Dual Trigger (GnRH Agonist + Low-Dose hCG) Criteria and Dose
rule.source: Clinical Evidence & ESHRE/ASRM Consensus (Griffin 2014; Lin 2013; Ding 2020)
rule.population: Normal responders in GnRH antagonist protocol planning fresh transfer, or patients with previous low oocyte maturation rate (MII < 60%), POSEIDON groups, or poor responder cohorts.
rule.hormonalCriteria: Estradiol < 3,500 pg/mL, Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar pattern
rule.safetyCriteria: Moderate or low OHSS risk (avoid in severe hyper-responders with > 25 follicles)
rule.timingCriteria: Administer both agents simultaneously 35 to 37 hours prior to oocyte retrieval
rule.doseCriteria: GnRH Agonist (Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c.) PLUS low-dose hCG (1,000–1,500 IU s.c. or rhCG 65–125 µg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation cycles
Severe OHSS risk (E2 > 4,500 pg/mL or > 25 follicles) where all exogenous hCG must be avoided
exceptions: In high normal responders, the hCG component may be halved to 1,000 IU
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg + hCG 1,000–1,500 IU s.c. simultaneously 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh embryo transfer.
potentialAdvantages: Significantly increases percentage of mature metaphase II (MII) oocytes and usable blastocysts in suboptimal responders
Permits fresh embryo transfer with standard luteal support while lowering OHSS risk relative to full-dose hCG (10,000 IU)
potentialLimitations: Contains low-dose hCG, which retains small residual OHSS risk compared to pure agonist trigger in hyper-responders
safetyConsiderations: Do not use if trigger day Estradiol exceeds 4,000 pg/mL or total follicle count exceeds 22 follicles

sections.title: Protocol Selection & Ovarian Stimulation Plan
sections.summary: Available

fields.label: Primary recommendation
fields.value: GnRH antagonist protocol is strongly recommended for predicted high responders and PCOS patients (ESHRE 2025 Rec 14 / Grade A; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514). Antagonist protocols yield equivalent live birth rates compared to long agonist protocols while reducing moderate-to-severe OHSS by over 50%, and uniquely allow GnRH agonist triggering. Starting dose explicitly defaults to the 100–125 IU/day tier per ESHRE 2025 Rec 13. Routine delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 12), and estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended in antagonist protocols (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Long agonist protocols are contraindicated due to unmitigated OHSS risk. PPOS is an evidence-supported alternative (ESHRE 2025 Rec 24) when elective freeze-all or PGT-A is planned.

evidence.title: Usability and utility of the CONSORT calculator for FSH starting doses: a prospective observational study
evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre observational study (197 women, 45 French centres) of the CONSORT calculator in routine practice. Full text uploaded and verified: it confirms the four calculator inputs (age, BMI, cycle day 2-4 basal FSH, AFC of follicles >=2 mm and <11 mm), the recommendation range of 112.5-450 IU in 37.5 IU increments, and that the calculator was delivered as a password-protected website rather than a printed table. It prints NO variable bands, NO point assignments and NO score-to-dose crosswalk. Usability was high (97.8% of physicians) but the recommendation was followed for only 45.2% of patients; mean CONSORT dose 119.7 IU versus 163.9 IU planned and 151.7 IU prescribed.

recommendation.message: GnRH antagonist protocol recommended for poor ovarian responder / POSEIDON profile.

explanation.clinicalRationale: GnRH antagonist protocol is recommended for predicted poor responders, POSEIDON groups, and Bologna criteria (ESHRE 2025 Rec 18, 22; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018). The antagonist avoids profound pituitary downregulation and heavy suppression of early follicular recruitment, reducing stimulation duration and gonadotropin consumption with equivalent live birth rates. Starting dose is strictly capped at the 300 IU/day hard ceiling per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20 (Strong recommendation, High Quality). Delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 17), and routine estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Microflare (short agonist flare) is an alternative to utilize endogenous flare. In very low reserve, modified natural cycle may be considered per ESHRE 2025 Rec 19 (GPP).
explanation.publication: Human Reproduction (doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018; PMID: 39982461) / Fertility and Sterility
explanation.notes: Starting dose ceiling capped at 300 IU/day per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20. Heavy downregulation with long agonist is not recommended.

selection.message: Highly purified hMG (hp-hMG) or r-hFSH with r-hLH recommended for advanced reproductive age (≥35 years) and poor ovarian reserve.
selection.lhStrategy: LH supplementation (via hp-hMG or r-hLH addition) is equally recommended to r-hFSH alone for women of advanced age (≥35 years) and low responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 29, 30). Compensates for age-related decline in theca-cell LH sensitivity.
negativeRecommendations: Do NOT combine r-hFSH and hMG concurrently in the same stimulation phase (ESHRE 2025 Rec 31, Conditional, ⊕⊕).
A gonadotropin daily dose higher than 300 IU/day is NOT recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 20, Strong, ⊕).
Adding low dosages of hCG to FSH stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 36, Conditional, ⊕).
Routine letrozole addition is probably not recommended for low responders (ESHRE 2025 Rec 39, Conditional, ⊕⊕).

explanation.whySelected: Highly purified hMG (hp-hMG) is recommended as a preferred preparation for women of advanced reproductive age (≥35 years) and low ovarian reserve (POSEIDON Groups 2/4, Bologna POR). Provides dual FSH and LH/hCG activity in a single preparation. Recombinant FSH with r-hLH or fixed combination (2:1) is an equally recommended alternative (ESHRE 2025 Rec 25, 29, 30).
explanation.supportingPublication: Ata B. et al., Hum Reprod Open 2025; Alviggi C. et al., Front Endocrinol 2016
explanation.clinicalComments: Daily gonadotropin dose must not exceed 300 IU/day (ESHRE Rec 20). If mild stimulation is selected, clomiphene citrate alone or with gonadotropins is equally recommended (Rec 42). Routine growth hormone, DHEA, or testosterone are probably not recommended (Rec 47, 49, 50).

firedRule.ruleName: Steady Follicular Progression — Maintain Current Dose (ESHRE 2025 Rec 43)
firedRule.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation (2025 Update, Rec 43)
firedRule.population: Predicted normal responders and patients with steady follicular recruitment
firedRule.protocol: GnRH antagonist or GnRH agonist protocols
firedRule.threshold: Steady follicular cohort growth (4–15 follicles >= 10 mm, E2 progressing 150–300 pg/mL per mature follicle)
firedRule.action: Maintain current daily gonadotropin dose. Routine dose adjustment is not recommended per ESHRE 2025 Rec 43.
exceptions: Emergence of severe hyper-response or profound follicular arrest

registeredRules.ruleName: Hypo-Response / Slow Follicular Recruitment — Step-Up Titration (POSEIDON / ESHRE Rec 20)
registeredRules.source: POSEIDON Group Stratification (Alviggi et al., 2016) / ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.population: Suboptimal or slow responders on Day 5–8 of ovarian stimulation
registeredRules.gonadotropin: r-hFSH or hMG (or addition of LH activity)
registeredRules.threshold: Stimulation Day >= 5 with lead follicle < 10 mm OR <= 2 follicles >= 10 mm OR E2 < 180 pg/mL
registeredRules.action: Increase gonadotropin dose by +50 to +75 IU/day up to maximum ceiling of 300 IU/day (never exceed 300 IU/day per ESHRE Rec 20). If already at 300 IU/day, maintain dose and assess follicular viability.
exceptions: Patients already receiving 300 IU/day ceiling dose
contraindications: Doses > 300 IU/day are contraindicated per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.evidenceLevel: Level II (Strong recommendation for 300 IU ceiling)

registeredRules.ruleName: Excessive Follicular Cohort / Rapid Estradiol Surge — Step-Down / Coasting (ASRM 2016 / ESHRE 2025)
registeredRules.source: ASRM OHSS Prevention Guideline (2016) / ESHRE 2025 Guideline Update
registeredRules.population: Predicted high responders and patients exhibiting explosive follicular kinetics or OHSS hazard
registeredRules.threshold: >= 18 follicles >= 10 mm OR Estradiol > 3000 pg/mL on Day 6–8 (or > 4000 pg/mL approaching trigger)
registeredRules.action: Reduce daily gonadotropin dose by 25–50 IU/day (floor 75–100 IU/day). If E2 > 4000–5000 pg/mL, consider coasting for 1–2 days while continuing antagonist. Prepare GnRH agonist trigger and elective freeze-all.
registeredRules.doseChange: -25 to -50 IU/day (or coasting if E2 >= 4500 pg/mL)
exceptions: End of stimulation when follicles are already trigger-ready (>= 17 mm)
contraindications: Do not administer hCG trigger if E2 > 4000 pg/mL or > 18 follicles >= 11 mm; agonist trigger required

registeredRules.ruleName: Cohort Maturation Reached — Discontinue Gonadotropins & Trigger (ESHRE 2025 Rec 83/84)
registeredRules.source: ESHRE Ovarian Stimulation Guideline 2025 (Rec 83, 84)
registeredRules.population: All patients reaching follicular trigger criteria
registeredRules.threshold: >= 3 follicles >= 17 mm OR lead follicle >= 18 mm (or >= 17 mm in low prognosis)
registeredRules.action: Stimulation complete. Discontinue daily gonadotropin injections and proceed immediately to final oocyte maturation triggering.

rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist or Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocols
rule.hormonalCriteria: Concordant serum Estradiol (approx. 150–250 pg/mL per mature follicle ≥ 14 mm); Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar appearance for fresh embryo transfer
rule.safetyCriteria: Peak Estradiol < 3,000–3,500 pg/mL; < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm; absence of early OHSS symptoms
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 37 hours (standard 36 hours) prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Recombinant hCG (Choriogonadotropin alfa) 250 µg s.c. (equiv. ~6,500 IU) or urinary hCG 5,000–10,000 IU s.c. (10,000 IU for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
contraindications: High risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm)
History of severe early-onset OHSS
exceptions: Cases converted to elective freeze-all can receive hCG if agonist trigger is contraindicated (e.g. pituitary defect) with cabergoline prophylaxis
rule.action: Administer rhCG 250 µg s.c. 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh cleavage-stage or blastocyst transfer.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / High Quality RCT Evidence
potentialAdvantages: Gold standard for fresh embryo transfer with robust, well-established luteal phase support
Consistent LH receptor activation ensuring high oocyte maturation and blastulation rates in normal responders
potentialLimitations: Prolonged half-life (elimination half-life ~30–36 hours) sustained over 8–10 days
Significantly increases OHSS risk in hyper-responders due to continuous luteotropic VEGF production
safetyConsiderations: Strict avoidance in patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18 follicles ≥ 10 mm
Progesterone measurement recommended on trigger day to rule out premature luteinization (P4 ≥ 1.5 ng/mL)
rule.activationPoint: src/lib/engine/trigger.ts — activated with ESHRE 2025 and ASRM validated criteria.

rule.triggerRuleName: GnRH Agonist Trigger Criteria and Dose (OHSS Prevention)
rule.source: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
rule.publication: Cochrane Database Syst Rev / Fertil Steril
rule.population: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist protocol ONLY (intact, non-downregulated pituitary GnRH receptors required)
rule.hormonalCriteria: Peak Estradiol typically > 3,500 pg/mL or rapid follicular cohort proliferation
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial lining receptivity not primary concern due to planned total cryopreservation
rule.safetyCriteria: Virtually eliminates both early-onset and late-onset severe OHSS by inducing rapid luteolysis
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocol (pituitary receptors desensitized; will fail to elicit LH surge)
Hypothalamic hypogonadism (deficient endogenous gonadotropin stores)
exceptions: Fresh transfer can be performed only if low-dose hCG luteal rescue (1,500 IU) or intensive luteal phase support (high-dose progesterone + estradiol) is administered
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / Cochrane Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
potentialAdvantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
potentialLimitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)
rule.activationPoint: src/lib/engine/trigger.ts — activated with Cochrane 2014 & ESHRE 2025 criteria.

rule.triggerRuleName: Dual Trigger (GnRH Agonist + Low-Dose hCG) Criteria and Dose
rule.source: Clinical Evidence & ESHRE/ASRM Consensus (Griffin 2014; Lin 2013; Ding 2020)
rule.population: Normal responders in GnRH antagonist protocol planning fresh transfer, or patients with previous low oocyte maturation rate (MII < 60%), POSEIDON groups, or poor responder cohorts.
rule.hormonalCriteria: Estradiol < 3,500 pg/mL, Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar pattern
rule.safetyCriteria: Moderate or low OHSS risk (avoid in severe hyper-responders with > 25 follicles)
rule.timingCriteria: Administer both agents simultaneously 35 to 37 hours prior to oocyte retrieval
rule.doseCriteria: GnRH Agonist (Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c.) PLUS low-dose hCG (1,000–1,500 IU s.c. or rhCG 65–125 µg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation cycles
Severe OHSS risk (E2 > 4,500 pg/mL or > 25 follicles) where all exogenous hCG must be avoided
exceptions: In high normal responders, the hCG component may be halved to 1,000 IU
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg + hCG 1,000–1,500 IU s.c. simultaneously 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh embryo transfer.
potentialAdvantages: Significantly increases percentage of mature metaphase II (MII) oocytes and usable blastocysts in suboptimal responders
Permits fresh embryo transfer with standard luteal support while lowering OHSS risk relative to full-dose hCG (10,000 IU)
potentialLimitations: Contains low-dose hCG, which retains small residual OHSS risk compared to pure agonist trigger in hyper-responders
safetyConsiderations: Do not use if trigger day Estradiol exceeds 4,000 pg/mL or total follicle count exceeds 22 follicles

sections.summary: Available

fields.label: Primary recommendation
fields.value: GnRH antagonist protocol is recommended for predicted poor responders, POSEIDON groups, and Bologna criteria (ESHRE 2025 Rec 18, 22; Hum Reprod. 2026;41(4):498-514; doi: 10.1093/humrep/deag018). The antagonist avoids profound pituitary downregulation and heavy suppression of early follicular recruitment, reducing stimulation duration and gonadotropin consumption with equivalent live birth rates. Starting dose is strictly capped at the 300 IU/day hard ceiling per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20 (Strong recommendation, High Quality). Delayed-start ovarian stimulation is probably not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 17), and routine estrogen pre-treatment is not recommended (ESHRE 2025 Rec 6). Microflare (short agonist flare) is an alternative to utilize endogenous flare. In very low reserve, modified natural cycle may be considered per ESHRE 2025 Rec 19 (GPP).

evidence.title: A new more detailed stratification of low responders to ovarian stimulation: from a poor ovarian response to a low prognosis concept
authors: POSEIDON Group (Patient-Oriented Strategies Encompassing IndividualizeD Oocyte Number)
evidence.summary: Original POSEIDON statement defining the low-prognosis concept and the four groups based on female age (<35 vs ≥35 years), ovarian reserve markers (AFC ≥5 / AMH ≥1.2 ng/mL) and ovarian response to previous conventional stimulation (<4 oocytes = poor; 4-9 oocytes = suboptimal).

evidence.title: The novel POSEIDON stratification of 'Low prognosis patients in Assisted Reproductive Technology' and its proposed marker of successful outcome
evidence.summary: Detailed description of the POSEIDON stratification, including sub-groups 1a/1b and 2a/2b and the rationale for separating expected from unexpected low ovarian response.

evidence.title: ESHRE consensus on the definition of 'poor response' to ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization: the Bologna criteria
authors: ESHRE working group on Poor Ovarian Response Definition
evidence.summary: ESHRE consensus establishing a standardised definition of poor ovarian response for research and clinical reporting, based on advanced maternal age or a risk factor, a previous poor response and abnormal ovarian reserve testing.

evidence.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI
evidence.summary: European society guideline on ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI. The guideline development group formulated 84 recommendations answering 18 key questions covering pre-stimulation assessment, prediction of ovarian response, stimulation regimens, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering and luteal support.

evidence.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM Practice Committee opinion describing the available ovarian reserve tests, their performance characteristics and the limitations of using them to counsel patients.

evidence.title: Prevention and treatment of moderate and severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome: a guideline
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM guideline reviewing the evidence on identification of patients at risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and on the strategies studied for its prevention and management.

evidence.title: Ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI — ESHRE guideline, update 2025
authors: The ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation
evidence.publisher: Oxford University Press / European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology
evidence.summary: November 2025 update of the ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline. Structured in parts covering pre-stimulation evaluation (ovarian response and pregnancy prediction from AFC, AMH, basal FSH, inhibin B, oestradiol, progesterone, LH, age and BMI), pre-treatment therapies, stimulation regimens and gonadotrophin choice, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering, luteal phase support and cycle-cancellation considerations. Recommendation statements are transcribed into modules only after specialist review.

evidence.title: Gonadotrophin-releasing hormone antagonists for assisted reproductive technology
evidence.summary: Cochrane review comparing GnRH antagonist protocols with long GnRH agonist protocols across randomised trials, reporting live birth, ongoing pregnancy and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome outcomes.

evidence.title: Usability and utility of the CONSORT calculator for FSH starting doses: a prospective observational study
evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre observational study (197 women, 45 French centres) of the CONSORT calculator in routine practice. Full text uploaded and verified: it confirms the four calculator inputs (age, BMI, cycle day 2-4 basal FSH, AFC of follicles >=2 mm and <11 mm), the recommendation range of 112.5-450 IU in 37.5 IU increments, and that the calculator was delivered as a password-protected website rather than a printed table. It prints NO variable bands, NO point assignments and NO score-to-dose crosswalk. Usability was high (97.8% of physicians) but the recommendation was followed for only 45.2% of patients; mean CONSORT dose 119.7 IU versus 163.9 IU planned and 151.7 IU prescribed.

disclaimer: This application is an Evidence-Based Clinical Decision Support System.
It assists qualified fertility specialists by organizing clinical information, applying validated evidence-based algorithms where available, and presenting explainable outputs.
Clinical responsibility remains with the treating physician.

Algorithms that are marked "Evidence Algorithm Pending" have intentionally not been activated because the corresponding validated guideline tables or published algorithms have not yet been incorporated into the Evidence Library.

registeredRules.ruleName: Steady Follicular Progression — Maintain Current Dose (ESHRE 2025 Rec 43)
registeredRules.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation (2025 Update, Rec 43)
registeredRules.population: Predicted normal responders and patients with steady follicular recruitment
registeredRules.protocol: GnRH antagonist or GnRH agonist protocols
registeredRules.threshold: Steady follicular cohort growth (4–15 follicles >= 10 mm, E2 progressing 150–300 pg/mL per mature follicle)
registeredRules.action: Maintain current daily gonadotropin dose. Routine dose adjustment is not recommended per ESHRE 2025 Rec 43.
exceptions: Emergence of severe hyper-response or profound follicular arrest

registeredRules.ruleName: Hypo-Response / Slow Follicular Recruitment — Step-Up Titration (POSEIDON / ESHRE Rec 20)
registeredRules.source: POSEIDON Group Stratification (Alviggi et al., 2016) / ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.population: Suboptimal or slow responders on Day 5–8 of ovarian stimulation
registeredRules.gonadotropin: r-hFSH or hMG (or addition of LH activity)
registeredRules.threshold: Stimulation Day >= 5 with lead follicle < 10 mm OR <= 2 follicles >= 10 mm OR E2 < 180 pg/mL
registeredRules.action: Increase gonadotropin dose by +50 to +75 IU/day up to maximum ceiling of 300 IU/day (never exceed 300 IU/day per ESHRE Rec 20). If already at 300 IU/day, maintain dose and assess follicular viability.
exceptions: Patients already receiving 300 IU/day ceiling dose
contraindications: Doses > 300 IU/day are contraindicated per ESHRE 2025 Rec 20
registeredRules.evidenceLevel: Level II (Strong recommendation for 300 IU ceiling)

registeredRules.ruleName: Excessive Follicular Cohort / Rapid Estradiol Surge — Step-Down / Coasting (ASRM 2016 / ESHRE 2025)
registeredRules.source: ASRM OHSS Prevention Guideline (2016) / ESHRE 2025 Guideline Update
registeredRules.population: Predicted high responders and patients exhibiting explosive follicular kinetics or OHSS hazard
registeredRules.threshold: >= 18 follicles >= 10 mm OR Estradiol > 3000 pg/mL on Day 6–8 (or > 4000 pg/mL approaching trigger)
registeredRules.action: Reduce daily gonadotropin dose by 25–50 IU/day (floor 75–100 IU/day). If E2 > 4000–5000 pg/mL, consider coasting for 1–2 days while continuing antagonist. Prepare GnRH agonist trigger and elective freeze-all.
registeredRules.doseChange: -25 to -50 IU/day (or coasting if E2 >= 4500 pg/mL)
exceptions: End of stimulation when follicles are already trigger-ready (>= 17 mm)
contraindications: Do not administer hCG trigger if E2 > 4000 pg/mL or > 18 follicles >= 11 mm; agonist trigger required

registeredRules.ruleName: Cohort Maturation Reached — Discontinue Gonadotropins & Trigger (ESHRE 2025 Rec 83/84)
registeredRules.source: ESHRE Ovarian Stimulation Guideline 2025 (Rec 83, 84)
registeredRules.population: All patients reaching follicular trigger criteria
registeredRules.threshold: >= 3 follicles >= 17 mm OR lead follicle >= 18 mm (or >= 17 mm in low prognosis)
registeredRules.action: Stimulation complete. Discontinue daily gonadotropin injections and proceed immediately to final oocyte maturation triggering.

rule.triggerRuleName: hCG Trigger Criteria and Dose (Standard Final Maturation)
rule.source: ESHRE Guideline on Ovarian Stimulation 2020/2025; ASRM Guidelines
rule.population: Normal and expected poor ovarian responders with low OHSS risk (peak E2 < 3,000 pg/mL, < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm) undergoing fresh embryo transfer.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist or Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocols
rule.hormonalCriteria: Concordant serum Estradiol (approx. 150–250 pg/mL per mature follicle ≥ 14 mm); Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar appearance for fresh embryo transfer
rule.safetyCriteria: Peak Estradiol < 3,000–3,500 pg/mL; < 15 follicles ≥ 11 mm; absence of early OHSS symptoms
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 37 hours (standard 36 hours) prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Recombinant hCG (Choriogonadotropin alfa) 250 µg s.c. (equiv. ~6,500 IU) or urinary hCG 5,000–10,000 IU s.c. (10,000 IU for BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²)
contraindications: High risk of ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm)
History of severe early-onset OHSS
exceptions: Cases converted to elective freeze-all can receive hCG if agonist trigger is contraindicated (e.g. pituitary defect) with cabergoline prophylaxis
rule.action: Administer rhCG 250 µg s.c. 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh cleavage-stage or blastocyst transfer.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / High Quality RCT Evidence
potentialAdvantages: Gold standard for fresh embryo transfer with robust, well-established luteal phase support
Consistent LH receptor activation ensuring high oocyte maturation and blastulation rates in normal responders
potentialLimitations: Prolonged half-life (elimination half-life ~30–36 hours) sustained over 8–10 days
Significantly increases OHSS risk in hyper-responders due to continuous luteotropic VEGF production
safetyConsiderations: Strict avoidance in patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18 follicles ≥ 10 mm
Progesterone measurement recommended on trigger day to rule out premature luteinization (P4 ≥ 1.5 ng/mL)

rule.triggerRuleName: GnRH Agonist Trigger Criteria and Dose (OHSS Prevention)
rule.source: Cochrane Review (Youssef et al. 2014) & ASRM OHSS Prevention 2016 / ESHRE 2025 (Rec. 114, 120)
rule.publication: Cochrane Database Syst Rev / Fertil Steril
rule.population: Predicted high responders, PCOS patients, patients with peak E2 > 3,500 pg/mL or ≥ 18–20 follicles ≥ 11 mm, or planned elective freeze-all / PGT cycles.
rule.protocol: GnRH Antagonist protocol ONLY (intact, non-downregulated pituitary GnRH receptors required)
rule.hormonalCriteria: Peak Estradiol typically > 3,500 pg/mL or rapid follicular cohort proliferation
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial lining receptivity not primary concern due to planned total cryopreservation
rule.safetyCriteria: Virtually eliminates both early-onset and late-onset severe OHSS by inducing rapid luteolysis
rule.timingCriteria: Administer 35 to 36 hours prior to planned oocyte retrieval (OPU)
rule.doseCriteria: Triptorelin acetate 0.2 mg s.c. (or Leuprolide acetate 1.0–2.0 mg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation protocol (pituitary receptors desensitized; will fail to elicit LH surge)
Hypothalamic hypogonadism (deficient endogenous gonadotropin stores)
exceptions: Fresh transfer can be performed only if low-dose hCG luteal rescue (1,500 IU) or intensive luteal phase support (high-dose progesterone + estradiol) is administered
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c. 35–36 hours prior to retrieval. Implement mandatory elective freeze-all segmentation strategy.
rule.evidenceLevel: Grade A / Cochrane Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis
potentialAdvantages: Complete elimination of severe OHSS risk through short-lived endogenous surge (LH surge ~24h vs hCG 8–10 days)
Induces physiological simultaneous FSH surge promoting LH receptor expression on granulosa cells and optimal cumulus expansion
Excellent oocyte yield and high maturity (MII) rate
potentialLimitations: Profound luteal phase insufficiency with luteolysis within 48–72 hours
Fresh embryo transfer without intensive modified luteal rescue results in significantly lower pregnancy and higher miscarriage rates
safetyConsiderations: Verify serum LH and progesterone 8–12 hours post-trigger if hypothalamic response is questionable
Mandatory freeze-all strategy strongly advised in hyper-responders (ESHRE Rec. 114)

rule.triggerRuleName: Dual Trigger (GnRH Agonist + Low-Dose hCG) Criteria and Dose
rule.source: Clinical Evidence & ESHRE/ASRM Consensus (Griffin 2014; Lin 2013; Ding 2020)
rule.population: Normal responders in GnRH antagonist protocol planning fresh transfer, or patients with previous low oocyte maturation rate (MII < 60%), POSEIDON groups, or poor responder cohorts.
rule.hormonalCriteria: Estradiol < 3,500 pg/mL, Progesterone < 1.5 ng/mL on trigger day
rule.endometrialCriteria: Endometrial thickness ≥ 7.0 mm with trilaminar pattern
rule.safetyCriteria: Moderate or low OHSS risk (avoid in severe hyper-responders with > 25 follicles)
rule.timingCriteria: Administer both agents simultaneously 35 to 37 hours prior to oocyte retrieval
rule.doseCriteria: GnRH Agonist (Triptorelin 0.2 mg s.c.) PLUS low-dose hCG (1,000–1,500 IU s.c. or rhCG 65–125 µg s.c.)
contraindications: Long GnRH Agonist down-regulation cycles
Severe OHSS risk (E2 > 4,500 pg/mL or > 25 follicles) where all exogenous hCG must be avoided
exceptions: In high normal responders, the hCG component may be halved to 1,000 IU
rule.action: Administer Triptorelin 0.2 mg + hCG 1,000–1,500 IU s.c. simultaneously 36 hours prior to retrieval. Proceed with planned fresh embryo transfer.
potentialAdvantages: Significantly increases percentage of mature metaphase II (MII) oocytes and usable blastocysts in suboptimal responders
Permits fresh embryo transfer with standard luteal support while lowering OHSS risk relative to full-dose hCG (10,000 IU)
potentialLimitations: Contains low-dose hCG, which retains small residual OHSS risk compared to pure agonist trigger in hyper-responders
safetyConsiderations: Do not use if trigger day Estradiol exceeds 4,000 pg/mL or total follicle count exceeds 22 follicles
rule.activationPoint: src/lib/engine/trigger.ts — activated with dual-trigger clinical RCT evidence.

evidence.title: A new more detailed stratification of low responders to ovarian stimulation: from a poor ovarian response to a low prognosis concept
authors: POSEIDON Group (Patient-Oriented Strategies Encompassing IndividualizeD Oocyte Number)
evidence.summary: Original POSEIDON statement defining the low-prognosis concept and the four groups based on female age (<35 vs ≥35 years), ovarian reserve markers (AFC ≥5 / AMH ≥1.2 ng/mL) and ovarian response to previous conventional stimulation (<4 oocytes = poor; 4-9 oocytes = suboptimal).

evidence.title: The novel POSEIDON stratification of 'Low prognosis patients in Assisted Reproductive Technology' and its proposed marker of successful outcome
evidence.summary: Detailed description of the POSEIDON stratification, including sub-groups 1a/1b and 2a/2b and the rationale for separating expected from unexpected low ovarian response.

evidence.title: ESHRE consensus on the definition of 'poor response' to ovarian stimulation for in vitro fertilization: the Bologna criteria
authors: ESHRE working group on Poor Ovarian Response Definition
evidence.summary: ESHRE consensus establishing a standardised definition of poor ovarian response for research and clinical reporting, based on advanced maternal age or a risk factor, a previous poor response and abnormal ovarian reserve testing.

evidence.title: ESHRE guideline: ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI
evidence.summary: European society guideline on ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI. The guideline development group formulated 84 recommendations answering 18 key questions covering pre-stimulation assessment, prediction of ovarian response, stimulation regimens, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering and luteal support.

evidence.title: Testing and interpreting measures of ovarian reserve: a committee opinion
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM Practice Committee opinion describing the available ovarian reserve tests, their performance characteristics and the limitations of using them to counsel patients.

evidence.title: Prevention and treatment of moderate and severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome: a guideline
authors: Practice Committee of the American Society for Reproductive Medicine
evidence.summary: ASRM guideline reviewing the evidence on identification of patients at risk for ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome and on the strategies studied for its prevention and management.

evidence.title: Ovarian stimulation for IVF/ICSI — ESHRE guideline, update 2025
authors: The ESHRE Guideline Group on Ovarian Stimulation
evidence.publisher: Oxford University Press / European Society of Human Reproduction and Embryology
evidence.summary: November 2025 update of the ESHRE ovarian stimulation guideline. Structured in parts covering pre-stimulation evaluation (ovarian response and pregnancy prediction from AFC, AMH, basal FSH, inhibin B, oestradiol, progesterone, LH, age and BMI), pre-treatment therapies, stimulation regimens and gonadotrophin choice, adjuvant treatments, monitoring, triggering, luteal phase support and cycle-cancellation considerations. Recommendation statements are transcribed into modules only after specialist review.

evidence.title: Gonadotrophin-releasing hormone antagonists for assisted reproductive technology
evidence.summary: Cochrane review comparing GnRH antagonist protocols with long GnRH agonist protocols across randomised trials, reporting live birth, ongoing pregnancy and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome outcomes.

evidence.title: Usability and utility of the CONSORT calculator for FSH starting doses: a prospective observational study
evidence.summary: Prospective multicentre observational study (197 women, 45 French centres) of the CONSORT calculator in routine practice. Full text uploaded and verified: it confirms the four calculator inputs (age, BMI, cycle day 2-4 basal FSH, AFC of follicles >=2 mm and <11 mm), the recommendation range of 112.5-450 IU in 37.5 IU increments, and that the calculator was delivered as a password-protected website rather than a printed table. It prints NO variable bands, NO point assignments and NO score-to-dose crosswalk. Usability was high (97.8% of physicians) but the recommendation was followed for only 45.2% of patients; mean CONSORT dose 119.7 IU versus 163.9 IU planned and 151.7 IU prescribed.
